timecoded_text_to_speech.text: You are from the beautiful state of Washington and you came over here to New Jersey to participate
in our LVS of democracy 2022 on climate and energy issues.
What motivated you to take time out of the business schedule to do so?
Well, I think the opportunity to gather with other individuals from across the political
spectrum to talk about how we address some of the major issues that we face.
That really, I don't think that anyone can deny that climate change is a global problem.
So of course it would deserve a global team of people who are working together to come
up with some policy solutions that can be implemented.
So after the first day of intensive discussions and meetings, also with your German colleagues,
is there something which surprised you?
Something you already take away as a learning for your state?
Well, I have always thought that Germany was truly a leader, whether it was in water conservation
or energy conservation.
One thing that really surprised me though it shouldn't have is that the folks that we're
dealing with are the same people.
They share the same concerns.
They really, regardless of the idea that we don't speak the same language, we're all
elected officials who are representing people, some who are hesitant, some who are strongly
ready to go and ready for change.
And so it was surprising to me that the challenges that we face are basically the same.
So there have always been up and down in the sense of a relationship.
What would you recommend how to strengthen the German-American partnership?
I think what we need to do, at least on our side of the Atlantic, is really develop organizations
that remain focused on it.
It's easy when we're all here to say, oh, this is something we should do, but unless that
translates into ongoing behavior, it may fall by the wayside.
And I think on this issue, and candidly many other issues, it's just too important to
allow that.
So for us to do sort of the cadre building on in our respective states and keep the relationship
strong with the colleagues that we've met during the Aspen Institute, I think that we can
assure that what we've done here will continue to translate for stronger relations down the
road.
Thank you so very much.

youtube_description:
As part of Aspen Germany's Laboratories of Democracy Initiative, the 2022 cohort met in New Jersey from September 13 to September 17, 2022. Each year, the project brings together a group of German and U.S. state legislators for two study tours – one to Germany and one to the United States – and virtual meetings. The goal of the project is to promote values-based dialogue and exchange of ideas on common policy challenges at the subnational level. Climate and energy were at the forefront of the 2022 round of exchanges.

We used the opportunity to interview the participating state legislators from the United States and Germany 🇺🇸🇩🇪. Why are they involved in transatlantic relations? Why are they participating in this Aspen program? Why is the topic of climate and energy important to them and their work? What have they learned from this exchange and their visit to New Jersey?

🗣️ Watch the conversation between Senator Ann Rivers (R), Member of the Washington State Senate, and our Executive Director Dr. Stormy-Annika Mildner.

To learn more about the program, visit our website: https://www.aspeninstitute.de/events/laboratories-of-democracy-initiative-meeting-of-2022-cohort-in-new-jersey/.

The project is supported by the Transatlantic Program of the Federal Republic of Germany with funds from the European Recovery Program (ERP) of the Federal Ministry of Economics and Climate Protection (BMWK).
